reasons.plausibility: The hypothesis is circular: it proposes applying a boriding treatment to already 'boride-based' components to form a protective boride layer, without explaining what the starting material actually is or why an additional boride layer would be more protective than the base material itself.
reasons.testability: The proposed test is clear and includes a decisive falsification criterion (no significant reduction in mass loss or lack of a continuous protective layer), but the starting material is so vaguely defined that the experiment cannot be practically set up.
reasons.usefulness: The hypothesis is of little use because it essentially suggests 'add more boride to a boride component' without identifying a specific material, coating composition, or microstructural feature that would provide a novel or non-obvious improvement.
